comments.body:
No need to cast to a string here.  This results in the LocalStorage value being `"true"`, rather than `true`.  If this value is changed to `"false"` (as opposed to `false`), the ui reducer cast to a boolean actually doesn't work as expected, because `Boolean('false')` is actually `true`.  The UI reducer as is here will actually return `true` for anything except `null`/`undefined`/`''` (the initial state), because any string that isn't empty is truthy.

I'm signing off because the behavior functions as expected, and requires someone to manually change the LocalStorage value for it to misbehave.

if we do `JSON.parse` of `getItem` then we will get `true` rather than `"true"`

we should parse a value from storage in any normal situation

Stringification of boolean `true` and string `'true'` produce different values, and so the `JSON.parse(stringified)` produces a different recovered value.

```
JSON.stringify(true)
"true"
JSON.stringify('true')
""true""
```

Try it out in your console.  In your case, because you stringified a string, you get back a string, which will always be truthy when cast to a bool.

yeah, JSON.stringify works as you said
but it doesn't work as `String` constructor does
https://prnt.sc/roq6rm

but now I understand your remark
at some point I have refactored `localStorage.setItem` for `LocalStorage.set` which does `JSON.stringify` under the hood. 
Yeah, I'll fix this in my next PR
thanks
